entries.note: "Nothing burger" is an evaluative label with no agreed threshold for what counts as an insignificant advance.

entries.test: Whether OpenAI had released a model called GPT-5 as of 2025-02-27.
entries.note: The plain reading is that GPT-5 was unreleased at the time of posting. "Fantasy" may also hint that it will never arrive, but the claim does not firmly say so.
This bundles a broad self-assessment ("pretty much everything I have told you was true") with the claim that scaling is not a physical law. Neither part has a shared test.

entries.test: Whether Tyler Cowen or similar AI commentators publicly blamed users for GPT-4.5's underwhelming reception.
entries.note: In the original, "they" could mean OpenAI rather than the influencers, so the proposition picks one reading he did not commit to. The part about others' hopes is a private state; only the forecast about blaming users can be graded.

entries.test: Reported profits of major AI labs and companies other than Nvidia as of February 2025, and whether GPT-5 had been released by then.
entries.note: "Viable business model" and "basically no moat" are vague. The parts about profits and GPT-5 have plain readings.

entries.test: Estimates of cumulative investment in LLM scaling by early 2025 compared with roughly twice the Apollo program's inflation-adjusted cost.
entries.note: It is framed as what a reasonable person would say, but Marcus endorses it. "Not that much to show for it" is vague, so the investment figure is the part that can be graded.
